newsitem.title: USA: Netcom names Yost as president, COO.
newsitem.headline: Netcom names Yost as president, COO.

text.p: Netcom On-Line Communication Services Inc said it has appointed Dan Yost to the newly created position of president and chief operating officer responsible for managing Netcom's domestic operations.

Yost, who has been president of AT&T Corp.'s AT&T Wireless Services eight-state southwest region, will start with Netcom in July and will report directly to Netcom Chairman and CEO David Garrison, the company said in a statement.

Yost, 48, has worked for telecommunications and technology industry giants AT&T, McCaw Cellular, which AT&T bought to create AT&T Wireless, and MetroCel Cellular, a Dallas, Texas-based wireless company he founded in 1985.

Yost said in a statement Netcom had developed "a strategic suite of Internet products and services," aimed at small and medium-sized businesses. Netcom earlier this year unveiled its plan to move away from the flat-rate consumer market and concentrate on value-added business products.
"He appears to have the right credentials to make a significant contribution to Netcom," said Charles Finnie, an analyst at San Francisco-based Volpe Brown Whelan & Co.
Finnie, who has a strong buy rating on Netcom, noted the stock has doubled since March 19 to close Monday at 16-3/4, up 1/4 on the session.
He said the stock has rebounded as investors "recognize this is a bandwidth-constrained world," where higher performance Internet access and services will draw a premium.
The stock is off sharply from its high of 82-3/4 in mid-November 1995, however.

Recently, the Internet access sector has been boosted by acquisitions, with one analyst predicting consolidation will slash the number of providers of Internet service by the year 2000, to 400 from around 4,000 now.
Intermedia Communications said two weeks ago it would buy Digex for about $150 million and last month GTE Corp said it would buy BBN Corp for $616 million.
